claims.text: An active-learning machine-learning surrogate can be trained on a modest set of high-fidelity ab initio evaluations.
The surrogate will accurately predict fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The surrogate will retain vibrational, anharmonic, and electron–vibration entropy contributions.
The proposed workflow will cost substantially less than explicit ab initio molecular dynamics or TOR-TILD.
The initial target systems are elemental and binary alloys such as Ta-Cr and Ta-V in solid and liquid states near their fusion temperatures.
Active learning on a limited but representative dataset can replace full-scale explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics evaluations of both phases.
The method should first be demonstrated on elemental and binary alloys with ample ab initio data and later extended to multicomponent systems.
A successful surrogate must faithfully capture phonon spectra and anharmonicity in the relevant phases.
A successful surrogate must faithfully capture electron–vibration coupling in the relevant phases.
Phonon spectra, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling govern important entropy contributions in crystalline and liquid states.
Configurational entropy can govern high-temperature phase behavior.
The model can learn the relevant energy landscapes and entropy terms from a curated subset of ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations.
Learning these energy landscapes will permit reliable phase free-energy predictions without extensive molecular-dynamics sampling across the phase boundary.
Predicted phase free energies and fusion points will be within approximately 5% of explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics values.
The method will reduce computational time by roughly a factor of ten relative to TOR-TILD.
Availability of ab initio molecular-dynamics training data bounds the method's expected applicability.
Transfer to highly complex multicomponent high-entropy alloys requires additional validation.
Complex liquid-phase electron–vibration coupling and extreme anharmonicity may prevent the surrogate from attaining the predicted accuracy in multicomponent systems.
Deviation by more than approximately 5% from the ab initio molecular-dynamics benchmark would falsify the accuracy hypothesis.
Failure to achieve at least a tenfold cost reduction relative to TOR-TILD would falsify the efficiency hypothesis.
